text:
At sunset, the merry girl
returns from the countryside
with her bundle of grass and flowering branch,
where violet and rose shine side by side.
Innocently she prepares it
to adorn her breast and hair
with joy when the festival comes.

Beside her neighbor,
an old woman sits spinning at her door,
her face turned toward the setting sun.
Her thoughts return to a far-off season
when, still a fresh young maiden,
she danced at the week's end
with the friends of her fairest years.

The air grows dark,
the horizons take on blue,
and shadows descend from the mountains
as the pale moon appears.
The village tower announces the festival,
and its cheerful chimes descend
to comfort every heart.

In the square a lively band of boys,
shouting and leaping here and there,
raises a joyful, stirring din,
while the farmer comes home whistling
and, seated at his table,
delights in the rest ahead.

When silence deepens with the shadows
and every light dies out,
I hear the hammer striking steadily
in the workshop, where the craftsman strives
to finish his task
before morning breaks.

This is the loveliest
and the last day of the week.
Tomorrow boredom and sorrow will return,
and everyone will go back
to customary work.

O charming boy!
Your sweet, blossoming age
is like a day full of joy,
a clear and peaceful day
before the festival of your life.
Enjoy it, then, enjoy it! This season
of flowers is gentle.
I will say no more; but do not weep
if the festival you long for is delayed.

translation.title: At Sunset, the Merry Girl...
